While it has some issues, this game has a special place in my heart. Despite what some people think, this is certainly a Bioshock game. Beautiful visuals, but also the worst of humanity on display. While the gameplay is a bit different than the first two games, it has the same heart. You scavenge any and all items, complete many side tangents and quests- while also creatively using your plasmids/vigors.

The start of the game is certainly the high point, as the story does get a bit muddled. However, in my opinion, upon multiple playthroughs there's a LOT of foreshadowing, and it's very comprehensible once you start to connect the dots. The story makes a lot more sense to me now. However, for a first time player, it's not the easiest to process. Especially if you aren't willing to listen to all the audio logs and side tangents!

The games DLC are arguably better than the base game, it finds a good way of developing one of the main characters (Elizabeth) in a satisfying way while also giving a pretty enjoyable story.

Conclusively, the game has some rough edges, but it's very charming. The characters are interesting, the locations are great(despite some repetition). It's from that era of gaming right before scummy game practices took over, where it looks beautiful but it still has care put into it.

After all these years, the art direction on this game is still one of the best. A truly immersive world/story and superb gameplay.

Masterpiece!

***NOTE*** This Review has been edited to account for the release of all the season pass content and to get me the steam awards badge ***NOTE***

Game looks great, runs great, and is fun to play!

You develop an emotional connection to the characters and setting and will want to pick it up the moment you finish.

Gunplay is smooth, and with the Plas... I mean Vigors, you'll be able to do even more in combat.

And the Skyhook! Melee weapon and fast transport system all rolled into one, this little baby is quite an adequate replacement for your old wrench!

My one criticism is this game doesn't feel like it has as much to explore as the original Bioshock, it's very linear. You've got your one path do go down, you get to a 'hub', have your next path, then you get to a combat area. It plays very cleanly, but the exploration aspect has been minimalized here.

***EDIT*** Concerning the season pass content: When the game came out, we were promised three story DLC. In the end, we got one story DLC in two parts, and a non-story DLC with a handful of audio logs that fleshed out some of the characters a bit more. While the storyline of the DLC felt like a very appropriate farewell to the series, the season pass felt a little lacking in content for $30 ***EDIT***

At the end of day after taking my time and doing the main game plus DLCs there just wasn't enough there for me to recommend this game. It seems like it was more of a framework of a game that could've been expanded upon and made great. While it does have nice looking environments and levels, ultimately there was little character development or interaction with story characters other than a brief conversation. The main story is a confusing mess to say the least and many choices made by the creators just took me out of being invested in caring about the characters. The factions battling, your quest to deliver Elizabeth, the cultures, and gameplay was too simplified; they had good ideas just not enough material in them. Gameplay was mostly disappointing due to combat only being able to use 2 weapons with low ammo even if you upgraded them, which would push you towards swapping weapons because you ran out of bullets. Plasmids aren't as useful because the environment doesnt allow as much use of them to fight enemies as in Bioshock 1. I could give more of my opinion but that pretty much sums it up in the first sentence. It isnt a game I believe I would revisit for another playthrough unlike the first Bioshock from 2007. Bioshock Infinite is a technically good game with interesting ideas and environments but fails at making anything meaningful or memorable.

For anyone playing on a modern system, make sure you cap your frames per second to 60 or even 59, set vsync on and compatibility mode for Windows 7. This game glitches out badly with the UI in the game if frames exceed 60. You can't pick up objects, search containers or even quit the game once the bug hits and need to alt-tab out the game and restart the PC. It sometimes happens even with the above mentioned preventative measures, but much more rarely, but that is a minor nuisance to play this great game!

If you liked BioShock 1 and 2 for the gameplay, this game is a fine addition to the franchise. But if you liked BioShock 1 and 2 for the story, this one pales in comparison.

I feel like Infinite had a lot of potential, especially with its setting firmly rooted in extreme patriotism, evangelical zionism, Jim Crow-era white supremacy and segregation, and exploitation of the poor working class American...and then failed to deliver any meaningful or impactful story point, and actually UNDERCUT its own message by playing the "both sides are equally bad" card with Daisy. The twist at the end is certainly a twist, but it feels very unfulfilling. I honestly feel like the game's story suffers from severely wasted potential, and fails to deliver any meaningful or impactful story out of it. I walked away from the game thinking "wow, white christian evangelicals kinda suck, huh." Which, let's be honest, I've already known for YEARS.

But if you're just in it for all the cool sci-fi concepts and creative ways to kill people using magical alcoholic beverages, it runs smooth, looks great, and will probably slake your bloodlust for a while.

Otherwise? Not recommended.

When played in conjunction with the Buried at Sea DLC, this installment offers a very satisfying conclusion to the Bioshock saga. Highly recommended.

Pros:
+ Well-written, coherent story that provides a complete and fitting end to the Bioshock saga.
+ Excellent visuals with very few graphical glitches.
+ Varied gameplay - action in main story, stealth in DLC.
+ Intelligent companion is an asset rather than a liability.

Cons:
- Disappointing level design - lots of weaponary and powers available, but no real need to utilize them creatively.
- No puzzles.
- Autosave only, can be frustrating if you like to explore.

This is probably one of my favorite games of all time. From the intense action to the compelling narrative, and you can't forget the Lutece Siblings. This game is a prequel to the original BioShock Games, but is set in an entirely different universe. With that comes many gameplay changes from the BioShock you know and love. The horror aspect is all but gone, however BioShock Infinite is still gory as all hell. Plasmids are back, but better than ever. Not to mention the GUI overhaul (for the better). While the game is not long, I can guarantee that you will enjoy the time you spend playing it. After all, there's a reason critics are rating it in the mid-high 90s. All in all, the game is great and worth a try to anyone who doesn't mind gruesome imagery.

Don't get me wrong I like the gears of wars mechanics in some games and it's really fun, but I just didn't feel it right in this game. I actually just played the first Bioshock to make sure I didn't have the same feeling and yeah indeed it felt much better level designed, no dummy or fake objects just put in place randomly.. just a "real" world to explore with corridors, rooms and actual open spaces!

This is a masterpiece and must get. BioShock Infinite definitely has one of the best stories in video games, if it's story isn't the outright best. The setting, story, and game as a whole are remarkably innovative, unique, and thought-provoking. The characters are well developed and memorable. This is only exponentiated by the incredible voice acting work.

In addition, the world is meticulously arranged with interesting tidbits that develop the setting and reveal the historical context of the events in the game. Every little detail in the game is there for a reason and are well thought out.

The gameplay mechanics are, likewise, intricately designed. Players get to choose from a wide variety of firearms, in addition to "vigors" which act like magic spells and have a compounded effect whe used with certain weapons. Furthermore, there are also rails in the game that players can use to manuever around the city. The visuals in this game are also stunning, fitting perfectly with the city-in-the-clouds setting.

The result of all the aforementioned points put together is one of the best video games available on the market. Every avid video game enthusiast should play this game at least once, regardless of what genre you prefer. It's just that good.

reason.text: Negative reviews in this period focus on a forced 2K launcher added to an older game through a "quality of life" update.
Reviews say the launcher breaks mods and the Linux version, and an official announcement says 2K are aware of possible impacts from the recent update.

lines.F1: BioShock Infinite had a negative surge (far more negative reviews than usual, often called a review bomb), Sep 2022
lines.F2: Sep 2022: 19% positive across 1,084 reviews (879 negative), against a usual 91% positive and 25 negative a month
lines.R4: (negative review, 31h played) "A recent 'quality of life' update force-adds the 2K launcher to run in the background while playing the game (in addition to Steam). My life has so much more quality now. I'm just feeling the quality!! /s Oh, and apparently this forced update broke..."
lines.R7: (negative review, 33h played) "Adding 3rd party launcher to 9 year old single player game and masking it as Quality of Life update is a new low. Is it not enough that you can't make good games anymore, but you have to go back and corrupt our beloved games as well?"
lines.R11: (negative review, 26h played) "Don’t bother with this series. They added 2K DRM to this goated series. Just sail the high seas or buy off GOG."
lines.R14: (negative review, 44h played) "Great game that received a completely unnescessary update that introduced a launcher. This breaks mods and the Linux version of the game. Nobody asked for this."
lines.R15: (negative review, 36h played) "2K in their infinite wisdom decided to add a launcher drm/storefront over 9 years after the fact that broke the games for many players and made it a pain for anyone wanting to revisit them. Incompetence at it's finest."
lines.N1: 2022-09-02, Official announcement: Quality of Life Update - EDIT: 2K are aware of possible impacts related to the recent update and working to resolve. Our player's experience is paramount, and we'll update our community with more information as it becomes...

tldr.text: Very Positive (91%): players love the story and characters.
Gameplay and combat draw as many complaints as the story does.

details.text: New players are less positive than long-time players, at 76% against 92%.
A flagged wave of negative reviews sharply lowered one month's score, but recent reviews still sit at 84%, so it says little about buying today.
